references.text: Peter quotes directly from Deuteronomy 18:15-19 and applies it to Jesus as the promised prophet. He warns that anyone who does not listen to this prophet will be cut off from the people.
Stephen quotes Moses' prophecy about a coming prophet whom God would raise up, linking it to Jesus.

Jesus says that whoever rejects him and does not accept his words has a judge: the word he has spoken will condemn them on the last day. This reflects the warning in Deuteronomy that God will hold accountable those who do not listen.
The author warns that we cannot escape if we neglect such a great salvation, which was proclaimed by the Lord himself, echoing the warning to heed the prophet's words.
The warning of punishment for those who reject God's word through the Son parallels the warning in Deuteronomy about the consequences of not listening to the prophet.
The preceding context describes the promise of the prophet whom God will raise up and whom the people must listen to. Verse 19 gives the warning about the consequences of not listening.
The warning that anyone who does not humble themselves on the Day of Atonement will be cut off from their people shows the same principle that God demands obedience and holds people accountable.
Jesus says that Moses, in whom they placed their hope, will accuse them because they did not believe in him about whom Moses wrote. This connects to the prophecy and warning in Deuteronomy.
